added: #Connect the nipple to the lamp base. Whether your base is wooden or metal, it needs a nipple on top to connect to the socket. Hold the threaded nipple vertically in front of you. Thread the knurl washer (the one with ridges) onto the nipple followed by the rubber washer. Attach the nipple into the center channel of your lamp base and make sure the knurl washer is closest to the base. Keep about  {{convert|1/4|in|cm|adj=on}} between the top of the nipple and the washers.[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 4.jpg|center]]

added: #Drill a vertical hole through your lamp base. Attach a {{convert|3/8|in|cm|adj=on}} bit to an electric drill. In terms of length, make sure the bit is at least half the length of the base material. Now, drill a vertical hole through both sides of the base to meet in the middle. Afterward, you should have a hole straight through your material for the lamp wire. [[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 2.jpg|center]]

#Create a cord escape within {{convert|2|in|cm}} from the bottom of the lamp base. The cord escape will run the lamp cord from the base and connect to a plug. Attach a {{convert|3/8|in|cm|adj=on}} bit to an electric drill. Make sure the length is at least the radius of your lamp base. Hold the base steady with one hand and drill the hole horizontally through the base so that it meets the vertical center hole. [[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 3.jpg|center]]

added: #Purchase a plug suitable for your lamp's wiring. Take a look at your plug's cord: is it flat? If so you need to buy a clamp-style wire plug. But if it's round, you need to purchase a two-pronged wire plug. Head to your local hardware store and check out your options!<ref>https://www.thisoldhouse.com/electrical/21016561/how-to-rewire-a-lamp</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 6.jpg|center]]

#Strip {{convert|1/2|in|cm}} of wiring insulation from the ends. Insert each end of wiring between your wire strippers. #Reattach the socket to the socket cap. Slide the insulator tube that acts as the outer covering of the socket over the inner part of the socket. Be sure that it slides over the lamp switch. added: #Gather the necessary materials for your lamp. Head to your local hardware store or visit an online supplier. Either purchase a DIY lamp socket kit or purchase the following: a zinc-plated nipple about {{convert|8|in|cm}} long, light bulb, lamp cord, lamp base, plug, lampshade, socket, socket cap, harp, knurl washer, and a rubber washer.[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 1.jpg|center]]

#Connect your socket locknut to the nipple. Thread the locknut that comes with your socket base down the length of the nipple extending from the base. Make sure it rests securely against the base with the rubber washer between it.[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 5.jpg|center]]

#Run your cord through the base of the lamp and out through the nipple. Thread your cord into the hole at the base up through the center channel. Continue feeding it until it's through the nipple extending from the lamp body.[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 12.jpg|center]]

#Separate the top {{convert|2|in|cm}} of the lamp cord. Your cord is made of 2 wires connected together: one that is ribbed (neutral) and another that is smooth (hot). Pull them apart with your hands or—if they're tightly connected—use a pair of scissors to cut along the middle indent that separates them.[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 14.jpg|center]]

#Wrap the smooth wire around the brass screw. Just as you did with the silver screw, locate the brass screw on the side of the socket. Loosen it until there's a space between its tip and the socket. Now, wrap the wiring clockwise around it and retighten the screw.[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 18.jpg|center]]

added: #Gather the necessary materials for your lamp. Head to your local hardware store or visit an online supplier. Either purchase a DIY lamp socket kit or purchase the following: a zinc-plated nipple about {{convert|8|in|cm}} long, light bulb, lamp cord, lamp base, plug, lampshade, socket, socket cap, harp, knurl washer, and a rubber washer.<ref> http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 1.jpg|center]]

#Drill a vertical hole through your lamp base. Attach a {{convert|3/8|in|cm|adj=on}} bit to an electric drill. In terms of length, make sure the bit is at least half the length of the base material. Now, drill a vertical hole through both sides of the base to meet in the middle. Afterward, you should have a hole straight through your material for the lamp wire.<ref>https://ilikethatlamp.com/pages/how-to-make-a-lamp</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 2.jpg|center]]

#Create a cord escape within {{convert|2|in|cm}} from the bottom of the lamp base. The cord escape will run the lamp cord from the base and connect to a plug. Attach a {{convert|3/8|in|cm|adj=on}} bit to an electric drill. Make sure the length is at least the radius of your lamp base. Hold the base steady with one hand and drill the hole horizontally through the base so that it meets the vertical center hole.<ref>https://ilikethatlamp.com/pages/how-to-make-a-lamp</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 3.jpg|center]]

#Connect the nipple to the lamp base. Whether your base is wooden or metal, it needs a nipple on top to connect to the socket. Hold the threaded nipple vertically in front of you. Thread the knurl washer (the one with ridges) onto the nipple followed by the rubber washer. Attach the nipple into the center channel of your lamp base and make sure the knurl washer is closest to the base. Keep about  {{convert|1/4|in|cm|adj=on}} between the top of the nipple and the washers.<ref>https://ilikethatlamp.com/blogs/inspiration/how-to-wire-a-lamp-socket</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 4.jpg|center]]

#Connect your socket locknut to the nipple. Thread the locknut that comes with your socket base down the length of the nipple extending from the base. Make sure it rests securely against the base with the rubber washer between it.<ref> http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 5.jpg|center]]

#Purchase a plug suitable for your lamp's wiring. Take a look at your plug's cord: is it flat? If so you need to buy a clamp-style wire plug. But if it's round, you need to purchase a two-pronged wire plug. Head to your local hardware store and check out your options!<ref>https://www.thisoldhouse.com/how-to/how-to-rewire-lamp</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 6.jpg|center]]

#Unplug the lamp and disassemble it. Start by disconnecting your lamp from its power source. Now, remove the lampshade from the harp, which is the metal piece that surrounds the bulb and connects to the lampshade. Afterward, remove the harp and unscrew the light bulb from the socket base and remove it.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=22</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 7.jpg|center]]

#Unscrew the old socket and unhook its wires. Look closely at the old socket—where the lamp's power switch extends—and locate the word "Press". Use your thumb or forefinger to press firmly on this area while wiggling the socket apart. Loosen the screws where the wires are attached and unhook the wires from the socket.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=51</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 8.jpg|center]]

#Remove the socket cap from the lamp's body. The socket base contains a center hole with knotted wires extending from it. Untie the knotted wires and then pull the socket base upward so that the wires slide through the center hole.[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 9.jpg|center]]

#Twist the ends of the old wires to the ends of the new wires. After twisting them together, take a piece of electrical tape and wrap it around them to secure them. Don't apply too much tape—the wires need to fit through the hole running down the center pipe that leads to the base of the lamp.<ref> https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=70</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 10.jpg|center]]

#Pull the old cord through the base of the lamp to feed the new cord through. Pull on the old cord from the bottom of the lamp until the new cord appears. Now, pull on the old cord from the edge of the lamp base to bring the new cord through the channel. Leave about {{convert|6|in|cm}} of new cord exposed at the top of the lamp.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=93</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 11.jpg|center]]

#Run your cord through the base of the lamp and out through the nipple. Thread your cord into the hole at the base up through the center channel. Continue feeding it until it's through the nipple extending from the lamp body.<ref>http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 12.jpg|center]]

#Thread the cord through the socket cap and secure it. Once the cord extends from lamp's channel through the nipple, place the center hole of the socket cap over it. Bring the it down to the nipple extending from the lamp base and turn it clockwise until it's secure.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=110</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 13.jpg|center]]

#Separate the top {{convert|2|in|cm}} of the lamp cord. Your cord is made of 2 wires connected together: one that is ribbed (neutral) and another that is smooth (hot). Pull them apart with your hands or—if they're tightly connected—use a pair of scissors to cut along the middle indent that separates them.<ref>http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 14.jpg|center]]

#Tie an underwriter's knot into the 2 wires. Start by making a {{convert|1|in|cm|adj=on}} loop with each wire that points upward. Hold them together with your thumb, forefinger, and middle finger. Now, take the free ends of each wire and feed them through the loop of the opposite wire. Afterward, pull the ends outward to tighten the knot.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=122</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 15.jpg|center]]

#Strip {{convert|1/2|in|cm}} of wiring insulation from the ends. Insert each end of wiring between your wire strippers. Grip the handle at the {{convert|1/2|in|cm}} mark and pull upward to remove the insulation.<ref>https://www.thisoldhouse.com/how-to/how-to-rewire-lamp</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 16.jpg|center]]

#Wrap the ribbed wire around the silver screw. Locate the silver screw on the side of the socket. Loosen it with a screwdriver by turning it counterclockwise. Once there is enough space, wrap the ribbed wire clockwise around it. After it's firmly wrapped around the screw, retighten the screw.[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 17.jpg|center]]

#Wrap the smooth wire around the brass screw. Just as you did with the silver screw, locate the brass screw on the side of the socket. Loosen it until there's a space between its tip and the socket. Now, wrap the wiring clockwise around it and retighten the screw.<ref>http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 18.jpg|center]]

#Reattach the socket to the socket cap. Slide the insulator tube that acts as the outer covering of the socket over the inner part of the socket. Be sure that it slides over the lamp switch. Now, press the socket down into the socket cap—this may take a bit of effort.<ref>https://www.thisoldhouse.com/how-to/how-to-rewire-lamp</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 19.jpg|center]]

#Attach the plug to your lamp's wire. Make a clean cut at the end of your lamp's base wire using needlenose pliers. Remove the plug from its case and feed the wire through the hole in the base of the plug. Spread the prongs apart and feed the wire into the slot until it hits the end. Squeeze the prongs together until you feel the wire being pierced by the prongs. Now, push the plug into the case.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=189</ref>[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 20.jpg|center]]

#Assemble the lamp and connect it to a power source. First, replace the harp, which is the metal piece that connects to the lampshade and surrounds the bulb. Press its prongs together and attach it to the brackets of the socket base. Now, screw the lightbulb clockwise back into the socket and lay the lampshade over the harp. You can now connect your plug into a power source and turn it on.[[Image:Wire a Lamp Step 21.jpg|center]]

added: If your old lamp has gone haywire or you're building a new one from scratch, wiring it might seem a bit daunting. But with a little bit of DIY knowledge, you can purchase a new cord and plug and get everything up and running. You're going to start by either building a new lamp from scratch or disassembling your old lamp. Afterward, you can run your new wiring through the base and connect a new socket!

#Gather the necessary materials for your lamp. Head to your local hardware store or visit an online supplier. Either purchase a DIY lamp socket kit or purchase the following: a zinc plated nipple about {{convert|8|in|cm}} long, lamp cord, lamp base, plug, lampshade, socket, socket cap, harp, knurl washer, and a rubber washer.<ref> http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>
#*Each lamp cord is made of 2 wires stuck together: one with smooth insulation and one with ribbed insulation. Take note of each one for later on.
#*If you purchase a flat cord, use a clamp-style wire plug, For round wires, use a two-pronged wire plug.
#*Swap a metal lamp base with a piece of wood if you want a smaller table lamp. Select a piece about {{convert|2 to 3|ft|cm}} high and {{convert|2 to 3|ft|cm}} wide.

#Drill a vertical hole into your lamp base if it's wooden. Attach a {{convert|3/8|in|cm|adj=on}} bit to an electric drill. In terms of length, make sure the bit is at least half the length of the base material. Now, drill a vertical hole through both sides of the base to meet in the middle. Afterward, you should have a hole straight through your material for the lamp wire.<ref>https://ilikethatlamp.com/pages/how-to-make-a-lamp</ref>
#*Hold the wood steady with one hand as you drill the hole.

#Create a cord escape within {{convert|2|in|cm}} from the bottom of the wood lamp base. The cord escape will run the lamp cord from the base and connect to a plug. Attach a {{convert|3/8|in|cm|adj=on}} bit to an electric drill. Make sure the length is at least the radius of your lamp base. Hold the base steady with one hand and drill the hole horizontally through the base so that it meets the vertical center hole.<ref>https://ilikethatlamp.com/pages/how-to-make-a-lamp</ref>
#* Place your lamp base on a flat surface before drilling the cord escape.

#Connect the nipple to the lamp base. Whether your base is wooden or metal, it needs a nipple on top to connect to the socket. Hold the threaded nipple vertically in front of you. Thread the knurl washer (the one with ridges) onto the nipple followed by the rubber washer. Make sure there's about  {{convert|1/4|in|cm|adj=on}} between the top of the nipple and the washers.<ref>https://ilikethatlamp.com/blogs/inspiration/how-to-wire-a-lamp-socket</ref>

#Purchase a plug suitable for your lamp's wiring. Take a look at your plug's cord: is it flat? If so you need to buy a clamp-style wire plug. But if it's round, you need to purchase a two-pronged wire plug. Head to your local hardware store and check out your options!<ref>https://www.thisoldhouse.com/how-to/how-to-rewire-lamp</ref>
#*Ask employees at local hardware stores for suggestions based on your lamp. Provide them with a picture if possible.

#Run your cord through the base of the lamp and out through the nipple. Thread your cord into the hole at the base up through the center channel. Continue feeding it until it's through the nipple extending from the lamp body.<ref>http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>

#Thread the cord through the socket cap and secure it. Once the cord extends from lamp's channel through the nipple, place the center hole of the socket cap over it. Bring the it down to the nipple extending from the lamp base and turn it clockwise until it's secure.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=110</ref>

#Separate the top {{convert|2|in|cm}} of the lamp cord. Your cord is made of 2 wires connected together: one that is ribbed (neutral) and another that is smooth (hot). Pull them apart with your hands or—if they're tightly connected—use a pair of scissors to cut along the middle indent that separates them.<ref>http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>
#*Take note of each wire and make sure you can distinguish them before proceeding to the next step.

added: ===Building a Lamp from Scratch===

#Drill a vertical hole into your lamp base. Attach a {{convert|3/8|in|cm|adj=on}} bit to an electric drill. In terms of length, make sure the bit is at least half the length of the base material. Now, drill a vertical hole through both sides of the base to meet in the middle. Afterward, you should have a hole straight through your material for the lamp wire.<ref>https://ilikethatlamp.com/pages/how-to-make-a-lamp</ref>
#*Your base can be anything you want—a piece of wood, old books, use your imagination!

#Create a wire escape in your lamp base. Attach a {{convert|3/8|in|cm|adj=on}} bit to an electric drill. Make sure the length is at least the radius of your lamp material. Place your lamp base on a flat surface. Hold it steady with one hand and drill a hole horizontally through the base so that it meets the vertical center hole.<ref>https://ilikethatlamp.com/pages/how-to-make-a-lamp</ref>
#*To help guide your drill, draw a line with a straight edge on top of your lamp base extending from the center hole to its edge.

#Connect the nipple to the lamp base. Hold the threaded nipple vertically in front of you. Thread the knurl washer (the one with ridges) onto the nipple followed by the rubber washer. Make sure there's about  {{convert|1/4|in|cm|adj=on}} between the top of the nipple and the washers.<ref>https://ilikethatlamp.com/blogs/inspiration/how-to-wire-a-lamp-socket</ref>

#*Purchase a DIY lamp socket kit from online suppliers or purchase each part separately. If you buy your own nipple from a hardware store, select one that's zinc plated and about {{convert|8|in|cm}} long.

#Connect your socket locknut to the nipple. Thread the locknut that comes with your socket base down the length of the nipple extending from the base. Make sure it rests securely against the base with the rubber washer between it.<ref> http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>
#*There should be about {{convert|1/4|in|cm}} of the nipple extending from the lamp base to connect to the locknut. If there isn't, adjust the washers.
#*Don't remove the socket cap, which is what the socket connects to.

#Unscrew the old socket and unhook its wires. Look closely at the old socket—where the lamp's power switch extends—and locate the word "Press". Use your thumb or forefinger to press firmly on this area while wiggling the socket apart. Loosen the screws where the wires are attached and unhook the wires from the socket.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=51</ref>
#*Remove the insulating covers on your socket if it has any.
#*Never attempt this with the lamp connected to a power source.

#Remove the socket cap from the lamp's body. The socket base contains a center hole with knotted wires extending from it. Untie the knotted wires and then pull the socket base upward so that the wires slide through the center hole.
#*Hold the base of the lamp for support as you pull the socket cap off.

#Purchase a plug suitable for your lamp's wiring. Take a look at your plug's cord: is it flat? If so you need to buy a clamp-style wire plug. But if it's round, you need to purchase a two-pronged wire plug. Head to your local hardware store and check out your options!<ref>https://www.thisoldhouse.com/how-to/how-to-rewire-lamp</ref>
#*Ask employees at local hardware stores for suggestions based on your lamp. Provide them with a picture if possible.

#Run your cord through the base of the lamp and out through the nipple. Thread your wire into the hole at the base up through the center channel. Continue feeding it until it's through the nipple extending from the lamp body.<ref>http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>
#*If the cord ever gets stuck, pull it back {{convert|2 to 3|in|cm}} and then continue feeding it through.

#Thread the wire through the socket cap and secure it. Once the wire extends from lamp's channel through the nipple, place the center hole of the socket cap over it. Bring the it down to the nipple extending from the lamp base and turn it clockwise until it's secure.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=110</ref>
#*In some models, you'll have to place a locknut onto the nipple before attaching the socket cap.

#Separate the top {{convert|2|in|cm}} of the cord. Your cord has 2 wires connected together: one that is ribbed (neutral) and another that is smooth (hot). Pull them apart with your hands or—if they're tightly connected—use a pair of scissors to cut along the middle indent that separates them.<ref>http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>
#*Take note of each cord and make sure you can distinguish them before proceeding to the next step.

#Tie an underwriter's knot into the 2 wires. Start by making a {{convert|1|in|cm|adj=on}} loop with each wire that points upward. Hold them together with your thumb, forefinger, and middle finger. Now, take the free ends of each wire and feed them through the loop of the opposite wire. Afterward, pull the ends outward to tighten the knot.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=122</ref>

#Wrap the ribbed wire around the silver colored screw. Locate the silver screw on the side of the socket. Loosen it with a screwdriver by turning it counterclockwise. Once there is enough space, wrap the ribbed wire clockwise around it. After it's firmly wrapped around the screw, retighten the screw.

#Assemble the lamp and connect it to a power source. First, replace the harp, which is the metal piece that connects to the lampshade and surrounds the bulb. Press its prongs together and attach it to the brackets of the socket base. Now, screw the lightbulb clockwise back into the socket and lay the lampshade over the harp. You can now connect your plug into a power source and turn it on.
#*If your lamp doesn't work, double-check the wiring in the socket and plug and try again. Always remember to remove your lamp from a power source prior to doing this.

added: If your old lamp has gone haywire or you're building a new one from scratch, wiring it might seem a bit daunting. But with a little bit of DIY knowledge, you can purchase a new cord and plug and get everything up and running. Not only will you learn a bit about lamps, it's a fraction of the cost of paying for repairs or purchasing a new lamp.
===Disassembling an Old Lamp===

#Purchase a plug suitable for your lamp's wiring. Take a look at your plug's cord: is it flat? If so you need to buy a clamp-style wire plug. But if it's round, you need to purchase a two-pronged wire plug. Head to your local hardware store and check out your options!<ref>https://www.thisoldhouse.com/how-to/how-to-rewire-lamp</ref>

#Unplug the lamp and disassemble it. Start by disconnecting your lamp from its power source. Now, remove the lampshade from the harp, which is the metal piece that surrounds the bulb and connects to the lampshade. Afterward, remove the harp and unscrew the light bulb from the socket base and remove it.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=22</ref>
#*Don't remove the socket cap, which is what the socket base connects to.
#*After wrapping electrical tape around the wires, snip off the excess piece with scissors.
===Connecting the Wiring for New and Old Lamps===

#Run your cord through the base of the lamp if you're assembling a new one. If you're assembling a new lamp, this is essentially the starting point of your project. Thread your wire into the hole at the base up through the center pipe. Continue feeding it until it's through the socket cap.<ref>http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>
#*If the cord ever gets stuck, pull it back a {{convert|2 to 3|in|cm}} and then continue feeding it through.

#Thread the wire through the socket cap and secure it. Place the center hole of the socket cap over the cord and bring it down to the socket cap. Turn the cap clockwise until it's tight into the cap and then secure it with a screw.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=110</ref>
#*In some models, the socket cap is indistinguishable from the lamp's body. If this is the case, screw the cap right onto the lamp body.

#Separate the top {{convert|2|in|cm}} of the cord. Your cord should have two wires connected together: one that is ribbed (neutral) and another that is smooth (hot). Pull them apart with your hands or—if they're tightly connected—use a pair of scissors to cut along the middle indent that separates them.<ref>http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>
#*After tying the knot, pull the wire from the base of the lamp so that the knot lowers into the socket cap and there's no slack in the line.

#Wrap the ribbed wire around the silver colored screw. Locate the silver screw on the side of the socket. Loosen it screw with a screwdriver by turning it counterclockwise. Once there is enough space, wrap the ribbed wire clockwise around it. After it's firmly wrapped around the screw, retighten the screw.
#*Double-check that you haven't accidentally wrapped the wrong wire.

#Wrap the smooth wire around the brass colored screw. Just as you did with the silver screw, locate the brass screw on the side of the socket. Loosen it until there's a space between its tip and the socket. Now, wrap the wiring clockwise around it and retighten the screw.<ref>http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>
#*Double-check that none of the insulation is underneath the screw.

#Reattach the socket to the socket cap. Slide the insulator tube that acts as the outer covering of the socket over the inner part of the socket. Be sure that it slides over the lamp switch. Now, press the socket down into the socket cap—this may take a bit of effort.<ref>https://www.thisoldhouse.com/how-to/how-to-rewire-lamp</ref>
#*Listen for a click as you push the socket into the cap—once you hear it, it's firmly in place.

#Reassemble the lamp and connect it to a power source. First, replace the harp by pressing its prongs together and attach it to the brackets of the socket base. Screw the lightbulb back into the socket and lay the lampshade over the harp. Now, connect your plug into a power source and turn it on.
#*If your lamp doesn't work, double-check the wiring in the socket and plug and try again.

#*After wrapping electrical tape around the wires, snip off the excess piece with scissors instead of continuing to wrap it around.
===Connecting the New Wiring===

#Thread the new wire through the socket base and secure it. Place the center hole of the socket base over the new cord and bring it down to the socket cap. Turn the base clockwise until it's tight into the cap and then secure it with a screw.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=110</ref>
#*In some models, the socket cap is indistinguishable from the lamp's body. If this is the case, screw the base right onto the lamp body.

#Separate the top {{convert|2|in|cm}} of the new cord. Your new cord should have two wires connected together: one that is ribbed (neutral) and another that is smooth (hot). Pull them apart with your hands or—if they're tightly connected—use a pair of scissors.<ref>http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>
#*After tying the knot, pull the wire from the base of the lamp so that the knot lowers into the socket base and there's no slack in the line.

#Wrap the ribbed wire around the silver colored screw. Loosen the silver screw with a screwdriver by turning it counterclockwise. Once there is enough space, wrap the ribbed wire clockwise around it. After it's firmly wrapped around the screw, retighten the screw.
#*Doublecheck that you haven't accidentally wrapped the wrong wire.

#Wrap the smooth wire around the brass colored screw. Just as you did with the silver screw, loosen the brass colored screw until there's a space between its tip and the socket base. Now, wrap the wiring clockwise around it and retighten the screw.<ref>http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>
#*Doublecheck that none of the insulation is underneath the screw.
#Reattach the socket. Slide the insulator tube and the outer covering of the socket over the inner part of the socket. Be sure that it slides over the lamp switch. Now, the push socket onto the base
#*Listen for a click as you push the socket into the base—once you hear it, it's firmly in place.
#Reassemble the lamp and connect it to a power source. First replace the harp, then the lightbulb, and finally the lampshade. Now, connect your plug into a power source and turn it on.
#*If your lamp doesn't work, doublecheck the wiring in the socket base and plug and try again.

added: If your lamp wiring is at the end of its lifespan but the body still has some life left, don't buy a new one just yet! With a little bit of DIY knowledge, you can purchase a new cord and plug and wire it into your existing frame. Not only will you learn a bit about lamps, it's a fraction of the cost of buying a new one.
==Steps==
===Disassembling Your Old Lamp===

#Purchase a plug suitable for your lamp's wiring. Take a look at your plug's cord: is it flat or round? If so, you need to buy a clamp-style wire plug. But if it's round, you need to purchase a two-pronged wire plug. Head to your local hardware store and check out your options!<ref>https://www.thisoldhouse.com/how-to/how-to-rewire-lamp</ref>
#*Ask employees at local hardware stores for suggestions based on your lamp. Provide them with a picture if possible.

#Unplug the lamp and disassemble it. Start by disconnecting your lamp from its power source. Now, remove the lampshade, unscrew the light bulb, and remove the harp, which is the metal piece that surrounds the bulb and connects to the lampshade.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=22</ref>
#*Squeeze the 2 arms of the harp together to remove it from its brackets.

#Unscrew the old socket and unhook its wires. Look closely at the old socket and locate the word "Press". Use your thumb or forefinger to press firmly on this area while wiggling the socket apart. Loosen the screws where the wires are attached and unhook the wires from the socket.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=51</ref>
#*Remove the insulating covers on your socket base if it has any.

#Remove the socket base from the lamp's body. The socket base contains a center hole with knotted wires extending from it. Untie the knotted wires and then pull the socket base upward—the wires should slide through the center hole.
#*Hold the base of the lamp for support as you pull the socket base off.

#Twist the ends of the old wires to the ends of the new wires. After twisting them together, take a piece of electrical tape and wrap it around them to secure them. Don't apply too much tape—the wires need to fit through the hole running down the center pipe that leads to the base of the lamp.<ref> https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=70</ref>
#*After wrapping electrical tape around the wires, snip off the excess piece with scissors instead of continuing to wrap it around.

#Pull the old cord through the base of the lamp to feed the new cord through. Pull on the old cord from the bottom of the lamp until the new cord appears. Now, pull on the old cord from the edge of the lamp base to bring the new cord through the channel. Leave about {{convert|6|in|cm}} of new cord exposed at the top of the lamp.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=93</ref>
#*Discard the old cord once the new cord runs from the top of the lamp to outside of the lamp's base.
#*If your lamp's base is covered in felt, carefully cut around its perimeter with a paring knife and peel it off.
===Connecting the New Wiring===

#Thread the new wire through the socket base and secure it. Place the center hole of the socket base over the new cord and bring it down to the socket cap. Turn the base clockwise until it's tight into the cap and then secure it with a screw.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=110</ref>
#*In some models, the socket cap is indistinguishable from the lamp's body. If this is the case, screw the base right onto the lamp body.

#Separate the top {{convert|2|in|cm}} of the new cord. Your new cord should have two wires connected together: one that is ribbed (neutral) and another that is smooth (hot). Pull them apart with your hands or—if they're tightly connected—use a pair of scissors.<ref>http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>
#*Take note of each cord before proceeding to the next step.

#Tie an underwriter's knot into the 2 wires. Start by making a loop with each wire. Now, take the ends of each wire and feed them through the loop of the opposite wire. Afterward, pull the ends outward to tighten the knot.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=122</ref>
#*After tying the knot, pull the wire from the base of the lamp so that the knot lowers into the socket base and there's no slack in the line.
#*Cut the wires {{convert|2|in|cm}} from the knot when you're done.

#Strip {{convert|1/2|in|cm}} of wiring insulation from the ends. Insert each end of wiring between your wire strippers. Grip the handle at the {{convert|1/2|in|cm}} mark and pull upward to remove the insulation.<ref>https://www.thisoldhouse.com/how-to/how-to-rewire-lamp</ref>
#*Hold the wire insulation firmly with one hand as you pull the wire stripper upward.

#Wrap the ribbed wire around the silver colored screw. Loosen the silver screw with a screwdriver by turning it counterclockwise. Once there is enough space, wrap the ribbed wire clockwise around it. After it's firmly wrapped around the screw, retighten the screw.
#*Doublecheck that you haven't accidentally wrapped the wrong wire.
#*Make sure that none of the insulation is underneath the screw.

#Wrap the smooth wire around the brass colored screw. Just as you did with the silver screw, loosen the brass colored screw until there's a space between its tip and the socket base. Now, wrap the wiring clockwise around it and retighten the screw.<ref>http://scavengerchic.com/2014/10/17/how-to-wire-your-homemade-lamp-with-pictures/</ref>
#*Doublecheck that none of the insulation is underneath the screw.
#Reattach the socket. Slide the insulator tube and the outer covering of the socket over the inner part of the socket. Be sure that it slides over the lamp switch. Now, the push socket onto the base
#*Listen for a click as you push the socket into the base—once you hear it, it's firmly in place.

#Attach the plug to your lamp's wire. Make a clean cut at the end of your lamp's base wire using needlenose pliers. Remove the plug from its case and feed the wire through the hole in the base of the plug. Spread the prongs apart and feed the wire into the slot until it hits the end. Squeeze the prongs together until you feel the wire being pierced by the prongs. Now, push the plug into the case.<ref>https://youtu.be/1d720r9Er-0?t=189</ref>
#*Swap out needlenose pliers with wire cutters if you'd like.
#Reassemble the lamp and connect it to a power source. First replace the harp, then the lightbulb, and finally the lampshade. Now, connect your plug into a power source and turn it on.
#*If your lamp doesn't work, doublecheck the wiring in the socket base and plug and try again.
==Things You'll Need==
*Adjustable pliers
*Needlenose pliers
*Wire cutters
*Flathead Phillips screwdriver
*Electrical tape
*Lamp socket
*Lamp cord
*Quick clamp plug
